verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between Selgantolimod and Carboxypeptidase N catalytic chain, as both are targets of the Influenza B virus B/Hong Kong/259/2010 hemagglutinin antigen (MDCK cell derived, propiolactone inactivated). Selgantolimod is predicted to interact with Copper chaperone for superoxide dismutase, which in turn is a target of the hemagglutinin antigen. This indicates a chain of interactions where Selgantolimod may modulate the activity of the hemagglutinin antigen, which then affects Carboxypeptidase N catalytic chain. The high scores in both paths suggest a strong predictive relationship, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains unclear. The evidence supports a possible regulatory role of Selgantolimod in the functional activity of the hemagglutinin antigen, which could influence Carboxypeptidase N catalytic chain through a series of molecular interactions.
